```alloy
  (some c: Command | r->c in Ask.rel and p->c in Add.rel)
  and (p in Inside or (some d: Document | applies[p, d]))
}
```

```readings
calls: {1} [calls] {2} | {1} does not [call] {2}
```

### @term availability

<!-- statement-term-availability:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [command_1](#term-command):
>
> command_1 is available exactly when at least one of these holds:
> - command_1 is a command that the [checker](#term-checker) has of its own
> - an [inside plugin](#term-plugin) adds command_1
> - there are installed_plugin_1 and [document_1](#term-document) such that installed_plugin_1 [applies](#term-apply) to document_1 and adds command_1
<!-- statement-term-availability:end -->

```alloy
pred available[c: Command] {
  c in Core
  or (some p: Inside | p->c in Add.rel)
  or (some p: Installed, d: Document | applies[p, d] and p->c in Add.rel)
}
```

```readings
available: {1} is [available] | {1} is not [available]
```

### @term heading

> A heading is a line of a document that starts with hashes and opens a part of it.

A heading that gives a kind and a stem, such as `@spec a-leaf`, declares a unit. A heading that does not is a [section](#term-section). A heading inside a fenced block, or inside the index of the document, is no heading at all.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Heading {}
sig Declaring, Fenced, Indexed in Heading {}
one sig Declares { rel: Heading -> Unit }
```

```readings
noun Heading: [heading]
Declaring: {1} is a [heading] that gives a kind and a stem | {1} is not a [heading] that gives a kind and a stem
Fenced: {1} is a [heading] inside a fenced block | {1} is not a [heading] inside a fenced block
Indexed: {1} is a [heading] inside the index | {1} is not a [heading] inside the index
Declares.rel: {1} declares {2} | {1} does not declare {2}
```

### @term extent

> The extent of a unit is the part of the document from its heading up to the next heading of its level or above.

A plain heading ends the extent of the units above it, because it is a heading of its own level or above.

```alloy vocabulary
one sig Reaches { rel: Unit -> Unit }
one sig Ending { rel: Unit -> Section }
one sig Under { rel: Unit -> Section }
```

```readings
Reaches.rel: the heading of {1} lies in the [extent] of {2} | the heading of {1} does not lie in the [extent] of {2}
Ending.rel: the [extent] of {1} ends at {2} | the [extent] of {1} does not end at {2}
Under.rel: {1} comes after {2} | {1} does not come after {2}
```

### @term own-text

> The own text of a unit is the text between its heading and its first nested heading.

The checker takes the statement, the site line and the blocks of a unit from its own text. A unit nested in another keeps what it writes.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Text {}
one sig Owns { rel: Unit -> Text }
one sig Nested { rel: Unit -> Text }
one sig SiteLine { rel: Unit -> Site }
one sig NestedSiteLine { rel: Unit -> Site }
```

```readings
noun Text: [text]
Owns.rel: the [own text] of {1} holds {2} | the [own text] of {1} does not hold {2}
Nested.rel: the text of a unit nested in {1} holds {2} | the text of a unit nested in {1} does not hold {2}
SiteLine.rel: the [own text] of {1} has a site line that names {2} | the [own text] of {1} has no site line that names {2}
NestedSiteLine.rel: the text of a unit nested in {1} has a site line that names {2} | the text of a unit nested in {1} has no site line that names {2}
```

### @term fence

> A fence is a block of lines between two lines of backticks or tildes, which holds logic or a table of readings.

The first word after the opening fence is the language of the block, and the second is its role. A block with no language is prose. The checker reads a fence for the unit whose own text holds it.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Fence {}
sig Languaged, VocabularyWord, BoundsWord, ScenarioWord, VocabularyBlock, BoundsBlock, ScenarioBlock, UnitBlock, NoSecondWord, BodyBetween, OffsetRight in Fence {}
one sig Within { rel: Fence -> Unit }
one sig Blocks { rel: Unit -> Fence }
```

```readings
noun Fence: [fence]
Languaged: {1} is a [fence] that names a language | {1} is a [fence] that names no language
VocabularyWord: the second word of {1} is vocabulary | the second word of {1} is not vocabulary
BoundsWord: the second word of {1} is bounds | the second word of {1} is not bounds
ScenarioWord: the second word of {1} is scenario | the second word of {1} is not scenario
NoSecondWord: {1} has no second word that names a role | {1} has a second word that names a role
VocabularyBlock: {1} has the role of vocabulary | {1} does not have the role of vocabulary
BoundsBlock: {1} has the role of bounds | {1} does not have the role of bounds
ScenarioBlock: {1} has the role of scenario | {1} does not have the role of scenario
UnitBlock: {1} has the role of the formula of its unit | {1} does not have the role of the formula of its unit
BodyBetween: [checker](#term-checker) reads the body of {1} as the lines between its fences | [checker](#term-checker) does not read the body of {1} as the lines between its fences
OffsetRight: [checker](#term-checker) says where the body of {1} starts in the document | [checker](#term-checker) does not say where the body of {1} starts in the document
Within.rel: {1} lies in the own text of {2} | {1} does not lie in the own text of {2}
Blocks.rel: [checker](#term-checker) reads {2} as a block of {1} | [checker](#term-checker) does not read {2} as a block of {1}
```

## @axiom every-claim-says-what-it-follows-from

<!-- statement-axiom-every-claim-says-what-it-follows-from:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> All of these hold:
> - for every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
>   when unit_1 is [unfounded](#term-unfounded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for unit_1
> - for every unit_1:
>
>   when unit_1 is [miscited](#term-miscited), checker reports a finding for unit_1
> - for every unit_1:
>
>   when unit_1 is [circular](#term-circular), checker reports a finding for unit_1.
<!-- statement-axiom-every-claim-says-what-it-follows-from:end -->

A claim that cannot say why it holds gives the next reader no reason to keep it, or to change it with care. So a canon passes the check only when every claim [cites](#term-cite) what it follows from, and only what its kind may follow from. A unit that does not is [unfounded](#term-unfounded) or [miscited](#term-miscited), and the checker reports a [finding](#term-finding) for it.

A claim that follows from itself says no more than that it holds. A unit that is [circular](#term-circular) has a finding as well.

```alloy
(all u: Unit | unfounded[u] implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | miscited[u] implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | circular[u] implies u in Finding)
```

#### @spec an-unfounded-unit-is-freelancing

<!-- statement-spec-an-unfounded-unit-is-freelancing:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> when unit_1 is [unfounded](#term-unfounded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for unit_1.
<!-- statement-spec-an-unfounded-unit-is-freelancing:end -->

This follows because a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) is the finding for a claim that cites nothing it follows from.

```alloy
all u: Unit | unfounded[u] implies u in Freelancing
```

## @axiom a-known-defect-stays-in-sight

<!-- statement-axiom-a-known-defect-stays-in-sight:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> All of these hold:
> - for every [bug_1](#term-bug):
>
>   when bug_1 is [hidden](#term-hidden), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for bug_1
> - for every [conflict_1](#term-conflict):
>
>   when conflict_1 is hidden, checker reports a finding for conflict_1
> - for every [test_1](#term-test):
>
>   when test_1 is [misleading](#term-misleading), checker reports a finding for test_1.
<!-- statement-axiom-a-known-defect-stays-in-sight:end -->

A defect the canon knows of must stay where the next reader sees it, until it is fixed or the owner of the design rules on it. A bug or a conflict out of sight is [hidden](#term-hidden), and a [test](#term-test) whose outcome says nothing true about a defect is [misleading](#term-misleading). The checker reports a [finding](#term-finding) for each.

```alloy
(all b: Bug | hidden[b] implies b in Finding)
and (all c: Conflict | hidden[c] implies c in Finding)
and (all t: Test | misleading[t] implies t in Finding)
```

This follows because each way a bug is hidden has a finding of its own. A bug that [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue) has an [untracking](#term-untracking), and one that names an issue the [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know has a [mistracking](#term-mistracking). One that names an issue the tracker has closed has an [outdated tracking](#term-outdated-tracking), and one that is not [tested](#term-tested) has an [untesting](#term-untesting).

```alloy
all b: Bug | hidden[b] implies b in Finding
```

>
>   when claim_1 is [unguarded](#term-unguarded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for claim_1
> - for every [tag_1](#term-tag):
>
>   when tag_1 [names](#term-name) no [unit](#term-unit), checker reports a finding for tag_1
> - for every [test_1](#term-test):
>
>   when test_1 is [adrift](#term-adrift), checker reports a finding for test_1
> - for every [pointer_1](#term-pointer):
>
>   when pointer_1 names no [target](#term-target), checker reports a finding for pointer_1
> - for every unit_1:
>
>   when unit_1 is not [used](#term-used) and is not a [conflict](#term-conflict), checker reports a finding for unit_1
> - for every unit_1:
>
>   when a [trailer](#term-trailer) [follows](#term-follow) unit_1, checker reports a finding for unit_1
> - for every [document_1](#term-document):
>
>   when document_1 [holds](#term-hold) a unit and holds no [index](#term-index), checker reports a finding for document_1
> - for every document_1:
>
>   when document_1 holds an index that does not [match](#term-match) document_1, checker reports a finding for document_1
> - for every claim_1:
>
>   when claim_1 names a [site](#term-site) that no [source](#term-source) holds, checker reports a finding for claim_1
> - for every unit_1:
>
>   when unit_1 [repeats](#term-repeat) a unit, checker reports a finding for unit_1.
<!-- statement-axiom-a-canon-cannot-go-out-of-date-unnoticed:end -->

Documentation goes out of date because nothing checks it. A canon goes out of date unnoticed when a claim no test checks stops holding, or when a test stops saying which claim it checks. It goes out of date as well when a link no longer leads where it says. So every leaf claim is [tested](#term-tested), and every [test](#term-test) [checks](#term-check) a leaf through its [tags](#term-tag). A claim that is not is [unguarded](#term-unguarded), and a test that does not is [adrift](#term-adrift).

So too every [pointer](#term-pointer), [index](#term-index) and [site](#term-site) leads where it says, and every id names one unit.

```alloy
(all c: Claim | unguarded[c] implies c in Finding)
and (all g: Tag | (no u: Unit | g->u in Name.tag) implies g in Finding)
and (all t: Test | adrift[t] implies t in Finding)
and (all p: Pointer | (no x: Target | p->x in Name.pointer) implies p in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (not used[u] and u not in Conflict) implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (some t: Trailer | t->u in Follow.rel) implies u in Finding)
and (all d: Document | ((some u: Unit | d->u in Hold.units) and (no i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes)) implies d in Finding)
and (all d: Document | (some i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes and i->d not in Match.rel) implies d in Finding)
and (all c: Claim | (some s: Site | c->s in Name.site and (no r: Source | r->s in Hold.symbols)) implies c in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (some v: Unit | u->v in Repeat.rel) implies u in Finding)
```

#### @spec an-unguarded-claim-is-untested

<!-- statement-spec-an-unguarded-claim-is-untested:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [claim_1](#term-claim):
>
> when claim_1 is [unguarded](#term-unguarded), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untesting](#term-untesting) for claim_1.
<!-- statement-spec-an-unguarded-claim-is-untested:end -->

This follows because an [untesting](#term-untesting) is the finding for a leaf that no test checks.

```alloy
all c: Claim | unguarded[c] implies c in Untesting
```

#### @spec a-tag-names-a-unit

<!-- statement-spec-a-tag-names-a-unit:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [tag_1](#term-tag):
>
> when tag_1 [names](#term-name) no [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting](#term-rotting) for tag_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-tag-names-a-unit:end -->

This follows because a tag that names no unit checks nothing, and a [rotting](#term-rotting) is its finding. A tag rots when the unit it names is renamed or removed.

```alloy
all g: Tag | (no u: Unit | g->u in Name.tag) implies g in Rotting
```

#### @spec an-adrift-test-is-reported

<!-- statement-spec-an-adrift-test-is-reported:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [test_1](#term-test):
>
> when test_1 is [adrift](#term-adrift), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for test_1.
<!-- statement-spec-an-adrift-test-is-reported:end -->

This follows because each way a test is adrift has a finding of its own. A test that [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) has an [uncitation](#term-uncitation) when it [carries](#term-carry) no tag. It has a [misaiming](#term-misaiming) when it checks a unit that is no [claim](#term-claim). A test that checks a [refined](#term-refined) claim has an [overreach](#term-overreach).

```alloy
all t: Test | adrift[t] implies t in Finding
```

##### @spec a-declared-test-carries-a-tag

<!-- statement-spec-a-declared-test-carries-a-tag:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [test_1](#term-test):
>
> when [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) test_1 and test_1 [carries](#term-carry) no [tag](#term-tag), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [uncitation](#term-uncitation) for test_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-declared-test-carries-a-tag:end -->

```alloy
all t: Test | (t in Declared and (no g: Tag | t->g in Carry.rel)) implies t in Uncitation
```

##### @spec a-declared-test-checks-only-claims

<!-- statement-spec-a-declared-test-checks-only-claims:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [test_1](#term-test):
>
> when [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) test_1 and test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [claim](#term-claim), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misaiming](#term-misaiming) for test_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-declared-test-checks-only-claims:end -->

```alloy
all t: Test | (t in Declared and (some u: Unit | checks[t, u] and u not in Claim)) implies t in Misaiming
```

##### @spec a-test-checks-only-leaves

<!-- statement-spec-a-test-checks-only-leaves:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [test_1](#term-test):
>
> when test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [claim](#term-claim) that is [refined](#term-refined), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [overreach](#term-overreach) for test_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-test-checks-only-leaves:end -->

```alloy
all t: Test | (some c: Claim | checks[t, c] and refined[c]) implies t in Overreach
```

#### @spec a-pointer-names-a-target

<!-- statement-spec-a-pointer-names-a-target:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [pointer_1](#term-pointer):
>
> when pointer_1 [names](#term-name) no [target](#term-target), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting](#term-rotting) for pointer_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-pointer-names-a-target:end -->

This follows because a pointer that names no [target](#term-target) leads nowhere, and a [rotting](#term-rotting) is its finding. A pointer rots when the file or the unit it names is renamed or removed.

```alloy
all p: Pointer | (no x: Target | p->x in Name.pointer) implies p in Rotting
```

##### @bug a-file-pointer-is-not-checked

> When a file pointer names no target, checker reports no rotting for the file pointer.

The check of a pointer reads only a [fragment pointer](#term-fragment-pointer). A [file pointer](#term-file-pointer) to a file that no longer exists passes.

Issue: #3

#### @spec a-unit-is-declared-once

<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-is-declared-once:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> when unit_1 [repeats](#term-repeat) a unit, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting](#term-rotting) for unit_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-is-declared-once:end -->

This follows because a unit that [repeats](#term-repeat) another shares its id, so no pointer or tag can say which of the two it names.

```alloy
all u: Unit | (some v: Unit | u->v in Repeat.rel) implies u in Rotting
```

##### @bug a-unit-repeated-in-one-document-is-not-reported

> When a document holds a unit, and the document holds another unit that the unit repeats, checker reports no rotting for the unit.

The check of an id compares the documents that declare it. A unit declared twice in one document passes, and the checker reads only the later of the two.

Issue: #7

#### @spec a-unit-is-used

<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-is-used:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> when unit_1 is not [used](#term-used) and is not a [conflict](#term-conflict), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [orphaning](#term-orphaning) for unit_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-is-used:end -->

This follows because a unit nothing [uses](#term-used) can go out of date, and nothing that relies on it notices. An [orphaning](#term-orphaning) is its finding. A conflict is no part of the theory, only a record of where it fails, so nothing uses it.

```alloy
all u: Unit | (not used[u] and u not in Conflict) implies u in Orphaning
```

##### @bug a-link-in-a-code-span-uses-a-unit

> When a unit is not used, and a code span names the unit, checker reports no orphaning for the unit.

The check reads link syntax inside a [code span](#term-code-span) as a pointer. A unit that only a code span names passes as used. Link syntax in a code span that leads nowhere is reported as a rotting.

Issue: #5

#### @spec a-heading-ends-with-its-id

<!-- statement-spec-a-heading-ends-with-its-id:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> when a [trailer](#term-trailer) [follows](#term-follow) unit_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misanchoring](#term-misanchoring) for unit_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-heading-ends-with-its-id:end -->

This follows because a [trailer](#term-trailer) changes the anchor the page renders, so a pointer to the unit's id leads nowhere on the page. A [misanchoring](#term-misanchoring) is its finding.

```alloy
all u: Unit | (some t: Trailer | t->u in Follow.rel) implies u in Misanchoring
```

#### @spec a-document-holds-an-index

<!-- statement-spec-a-document-holds-an-index:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [document_1](#term-document):
>
> when document_1 [holds](#term-hold) a [unit](#term-unit) and holds no [index](#term-index), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misindexing](#term-misindexing) for document_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-document-holds-an-index:end -->

This follows because a [document](#term-document) with units and no [index](#term-index) has no generated list to check, and a [misindexing](#term-misindexing) is its finding.

```alloy
all d: Document | ((some u: Unit | d->u in Hold.units) and (no i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes)) implies d in Misindexing
```

#### @spec an-index-matches-its-document

<!-- statement-spec-an-index-matches-its-document:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [document_1](#term-document):
>
> when document_1 [holds](#term-hold) an [index](#term-index) that does not [match](#term-match) document_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misindexing](#term-misindexing) for document_1.
<!-- statement-spec-an-index-matches-its-document:end -->

This follows because an index that does not [match](#term-match) its document lists units or statements that are no longer there.

```alloy
all d: Document | (some i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes and i->d not in Match.rel) implies d in Misindexing
```

#### @spec a-site-is-held-by-a-source

<!-- statement-spec-a-site-is-held-by-a-source:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [claim_1](#term-claim):
>
> when claim_1 [names](#term-name) a [site](#term-site) that no [source](#term-source) [holds](#term-hold), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mislocation](#term-mislocation) for claim_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-site-is-held-by-a-source:end -->

This follows because a [site](#term-site) that no [source](#term-source) [holds](#term-hold) was renamed or removed, and a [mislocation](#term-mislocation) is its finding.

```alloy
all c: Claim | (some s: Site | c->s in Name.site and (no r: Source | r->s in Hold.symbols)) implies c in Mislocation
```

##### @bug a-site-named-in-a-comment-is-held

> When a claim names a site that no source holds, and a comment names the site, checker reports no mislocation for the claim.

The check of a site reads the whole text of the source. A symbol that the code no longer declares passes while a [comment](#term-comment) still holds its name. A comment that says what the symbol was renamed to is enough.

Issue: #4

#### @spec a-heading-with-a-kind-and-a-stem-declares-a-unit

<!-- statement-spec-a-heading-with-a-kind-and-a-stem-declares-a-unit:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [heading_1](#term-heading):
>
> when all of these hold:
> - heading_1 is a heading that gives a kind and a stem
> - heading_1 is not a heading inside a fenced block
> - heading_1 is not a heading inside the index
>
> then heading_1 declares a [unit](#term-unit).
<!-- statement-spec-a-heading-with-a-kind-and-a-stem-declares-a-unit:end -->

This follows because the id of a unit is its kind and its stem, and the heading is the one place that gives both.

```alloy
all h: Heading | (h in Declaring and h not in Fenced and h not in Indexed) implies (some u: Unit | h->u in Declares.rel)
```

#### @spec a-heading-in-a-fenced-block-declares-no-unit

<!-- statement-spec-a-heading-in-a-fenced-block-declares-no-unit:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [heading_1](#term-heading):
>
> when heading_1 is a heading inside a fenced block, heading_1 declares no [unit](#term-unit).
<!-- statement-spec-a-heading-in-a-fenced-block-declares-no-unit:end -->

This follows because a fenced block shows an example, and an example must not become a unit that a test can cite.

```alloy
all h: Heading | h in Fenced implies (no u: Unit | h->u in Declares.rel)
```

#### @spec a-heading-in-the-index-declares-no-unit

<!-- statement-spec-a-heading-in-the-index-declares-no-unit:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [heading_1](#term-heading):
>
> when heading_1 is a heading inside the index, heading_1 declares no [unit](#term-unit).
<!-- statement-spec-a-heading-in-the-index-declares-no-unit:end -->

This follows because the index lists every unit already. Reading it as units would give each id two units.

```alloy
all h: Heading | h in Indexed implies (no u: Unit | h->u in Declares.rel)
```

#### @spec a-unit-sits-in-the-closest-unit-whose-extent-holds-its-heading

<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-sits-in-the-closest-unit-whose-extent-holds-its-heading:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every unit_2:
>
> when all of these hold:
> - the heading of unit_1 lies in the [extent](#term-extent) of unit_2
> - there is no unit_3 such that the heading of unit_1 lies in the extent of unit_3 and the heading of unit_3 lies in the extent of unit_2
>
> then unit_1 [sits in](#term-sit) unit_2.
<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-sits-in-the-closest-unit-whose-extent-holds-its-heading:end -->

This follows because nesting is the citation of the unit above, and the unit above is the closest one that reaches the heading.

```alloy
all u: Unit, v: Unit | (u->v in Reaches.rel and (no w: Unit | u->w in Reaches.rel and w->v in Reaches.rel)) implies u->v in Sit.rel
```

#### @spec a-plain-heading-that-ends-the-extent-of-a-unit-keeps-later-units-out-of-it

<!-- statement-spec-a-plain-heading-that-ends-the-extent-of-a-unit-keeps-later-units-out-of-it:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every unit_2 and every [section_1](#term-section):
>
> when unit_1 comes after section_1 and the [extent](#term-extent) of unit_2 ends at section_1, unit_1 does not [sit in](#term-sit) unit_2.
<!-- statement-spec-a-plain-heading-that-ends-the-extent-of-a-unit-keeps-later-units-out-of-it:end -->

This follows because a plain heading starts a part of the document that is about something else. A unit below it does not derive from a unit above it.

```alloy
all u: Unit, v: Unit, s: Section | (u->s in Under.rel and v->s in Ending.rel) implies u->v not in Sit.rel
```

#### @spec a-unit-owns-only-the-text-before-its-first-nested-heading

<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-owns-only-the-text-before-its-first-nested-heading:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [text_1](#term-own-text):
>
> when the own text of unit_1 holds text_1, the text of a unit nested in unit_1 does not hold text_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-owns-only-the-text-before-its-first-nested-heading:end -->

This follows because what a nested unit writes is its own claim. The unit above does not make it.

```alloy
all u: Unit, t: Text | u->t in Owns.rel implies u->t not in Nested.rel
```

#### @spec a-site-line-in-the-own-text-names-the-site-of-its-unit

<!-- statement-spec-a-site-line-in-the-own-text-names-the-site-of-its-unit:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [site_1](#term-site):
>
> when the [own text](#term-own-text) of unit_1 has a site line that names site_1, unit_1 [names](#term-name) site_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-site-line-in-the-own-text-names-the-site-of-its-unit:end -->

This follows because a claim that answers for one place in the code names that place on a line of its own.

```alloy
all u: Unit, s: Site | u->s in SiteLine.rel implies u->s in Name.site
```

#### @spec a-site-line-of-a-nested-unit-names-no-site-of-the-unit-above

<!-- statement-spec-a-site-line-of-a-nested-unit-names-no-site-of-the-unit-above:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [site_1](#term-site):
>
> when all of these hold:
> - the text of a unit nested in unit_1 has a site line that names site_1
> - the [own text](#term-own-text) of unit_1 has no site line that names site_1
>
> then unit_1 does not [name](#term-name) site_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-site-line-of-a-nested-unit-names-no-site-of-the-unit-above:end -->

This follows because the nested unit is the one that answers for that place.

```alloy
all u: Unit, s: Site | (u->s in NestedSiteLine.rel and u->s not in SiteLine.rel) implies u->s not in Name.site
```

#### @spec an-extends-key-lists-the-documents-a-document-extends

<!-- statement-spec-an-extends-key-lists-the-documents-a-document-extends:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [document_1](#term-document) and every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [path_1](#term-extension) and every document_2:
>
> when all of these hold:
> - document_1 starts with frontmatter_1
> - frontmatter_1 lists the path path_1
> - the path path_1 leads to document_2
>
> then document_1 extends document_2.
<!-- statement-spec-an-extends-key-lists-the-documents-a-document-extends:end -->

This follows because a pointer into another document leads where it says only if the checker knows which documents the author means. The author says so in the document.

```alloy
all d: Document, f: Frontmatter, p: Path, e: Document | (d->f in Head.rel and f->p in Written.rel and p->e in Leads.rel) implies d->e in Extend.rel
```

#### @spec a-path-is-read-from-the-folder-of-the-document-that-lists-it

<!-- statement-spec-a-path-is-read-from-the-folder-of-the-document-that-lists-it:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [path_1](#term-extension):
>
> when path_1 is a path that a frontmatter lists, path_1 is read from the folder of the [document](#term-document) that lists it.
<!-- statement-spec-a-path-is-read-from-the-folder-of-the-document-that-lists-it:end -->

This follows because a link in a document leads from where the document is, and a path in its frontmatter means the same.

```alloy
all p: Path | p in Listed implies p in FromFolder
```

#### @spec a-document-is-context-for-the-documents-that-extend-it-and-for-theirs

<!-- statement-spec-a-document-is-context-for-the-documents-that-extend-it-and-for-theirs:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [document_1](#term-document) and every document_2 and every document_3:
>
> all of these hold:
> - when document_1 [extends](#term-extension) document_2, document_2 is context for document_1
> - when document_1 extends document_2 and document_3 is context for document_2, document_3 is context for document_1
<!-- statement-spec-a-document-is-context-for-the-documents-that-extend-it-and-for-theirs:end -->

This follows because a document that extends another takes in what that one takes in, and the author does not list it again.

```alloy
all d: Document, e: Document, g: Document | (d->e in Extend.rel implies d->e in Context.rel) and ((d->e in Extend.rel and e->g in Context.rel) implies d->g in Context.rel)
```

#### @spec a-unit-of-an-extended-document-is-not-reported-for-the-document-that-extends-it

<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-of-an-extended-document-is-not-reported-for-the-document-that-extends-it:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [document_1](#term-document) and every document_2 and every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> when all of these hold:
> - the project lists document_1 among the documents it checks
> - the project does not list document_2 among the documents it checks
> - document_2 is [context](#term-extension) for document_1
> - document_2 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1
>
> then [checker](#term-checker) reports no [finding](#term-finding) for unit_1.
<!-- statement-spec-a-unit-of-an-extended-document-is-not-reported-for-the-document-that-extends-it:end -->

This follows because the extended document is checked where it lives. A second report of the same unit would only make noise.

```alloy
all d: Document, e: Document, u: Unit | (d in Checked and e not in Checked and d->e in Context.rel and e->u in Hold.units) implies u not in Finding
```

#### @spec an-id-that-an-extended-document-declares-too-is-repeated

<!-- statement-spec-an-id-that-an-extended-document-declares-too-is-repeated:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [document_1](#term-document) and every document_2 and every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every unit_2:
>
> when all of these hold:
> - document_2 is [context](#term-extension) for document_1
> - document_1 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1
> - document_2 holds unit_2
> - unit_1 has the id of unit_2
>
> then unit_1 [repeats](#term-repeat) unit_2.
<!-- statement-spec-an-id-that-an-extended-document-declares-too-is-repeated:end -->

This follows because a pointer or a tag cannot say which of two units with one id it means. The checker reads an extended document together with the document that extends it.

```alloy
all d: Document, e: Document, u: Unit, v: Unit | (d->e in Context.rel and d->u in Hold.units and e->v in Hold.units and u->v in SameId.rel) implies u->v in Repeat.rel
```

#### @spec the-statement-of-a-unit-is-the-blockquote-that-opens-its-own-text

<!-- statement-spec-the-statement-of-a-unit-is-the-blockquote-that-opens-its-own-text:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> when the own text of unit_1 opens with a blockquote, unit_1 has a [statement](#term-statement).
<!-- statement-spec-the-statement-of-a-unit-is-the-blockquote-that-opens-its-own-text:end -->

This follows because a reader looks for the claim of a unit right under its heading. The quote under the heading is what the unit says.

```alloy
all u: Unit | u in OpensWithQuote implies u in Stated
```

#### @spec every-line-of-the-blockquote-is-part-of-the-statement

<!-- statement-spec-every-line-of-the-blockquote-is-part-of-the-statement:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):

## @axiom a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently

<!-- statement-axiom-a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [run_1](#term-run):
>
> when at least one of these holds:
> - there are [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin) such that frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1
> - there is a [document_1](#term-document) such that [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a frontmatter it cannot read
> - run_1 asks for a [command](#term-command) that is not [available](#term-availability)
> - run_1 gets code 2 from a plugin
>
> then run_1 exits with code 2.
<!-- statement-axiom-a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently:end -->

A project asks for its checks in its documents: the plugins a document names, and the command it runs. A check that the project asks for either runs, or the author hears that it could not. Otherwise a mistake as small as a misspelled key turns a check off, and the author trusts a canon that nothing has checked.

So a [run](#term-run) that asks for what the checker cannot deliver exits with code 2. Code 2 stands above a finding and above success. Four things ask for too much. One is a [plugin](#term-plugin) the project lacks. Another is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) the checker cannot read. The others are a [command](#term-command) that nothing adds, and a plugin that could not run.

```alloy
all r: Run | ((some f: Frontmatter, p: Missing | lists[f, p]) or (some d: Document | d in Unreadable) or (some c: Command | r->c in Ask.rel and not available[c]) or (some p: Plugin | r->p in Return.code2)) implies r in Exits2
```

<!-- statement-scenario-1-axiom-a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> It must be possible that:
>
> There are [run_1](#term-run) and [installed_plugin_1](#term-plugin) and [document_1](#term-document) and [listing_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) such that all of these hold:
> - document_1 starts with listing_frontmatter_1
> - listing_frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) installed_plugin_1
> - [checker](#term-checker) runs installed_plugin_1 over document_1
> - run_1 [calls](#term-call) installed_plugin_1
> - run_1 gets code 1 from installed_plugin_1
> - run_1 exits with code 1
<!-- statement-scenario-1-axiom-a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently:end -->

```alloy scenario
some r: Run, p: Installed, d: Document, f: Listing | d->f in Head.rel and lists[f, p] and p->d in Over.rel and calls[r, p] and r->p in Return.code1 and r in Exits1
```

<!-- statement-scenario-2-axiom-a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> It must be possible that:
>
> There are [run_1](#term-run) and [document_1](#term-document) and [refused_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) such that all of these hold:
> - document_1 starts with refused_frontmatter_1
> - [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a frontmatter it cannot read
> - run_1 exits with code 2
<!-- statement-scenario-2-axiom-a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently:end -->

```alloy scenario
some r: Run, d: Document, f: Refused | d->f in Head.rel and d in Unreadable and r in Exits2
```

#### @spec a-document-gets-the-plugins-it-asks-for

<!-- statement-spec-a-document-gets-the-plugins-it-asks-for:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document):
>
> all of these hold:
> - when plugin_1 [applies](#term-apply) to document_1, [checker](#term-checker) runs plugin_1 over document_1
> - when the command line of a [run](#term-run) does not name document_1 and checker runs plugin_1 over document_1, plugin_1 applies to document_1
<!-- statement-spec-a-document-gets-the-plugins-it-asks-for:end -->

This follows because the plugins a document names are the checks it asks for. It gets those and no others. A plugin it did not ask for adds no finding, and one it asked for is not left out. A document that names none gets the plugins inside the package, as every document did before documents could name plugins.

```alloy
all p: Plugin, d: Document | (applies[p, d] implies p->d in Over.rel) and ((d not in Given and p->d in Over.rel) implies applies[p, d])
```

This follows because such a document asks for nothing in particular. It still gets the checks that every document got before documents could ask.

#### @spec a-flawed-frontmatter-is-refused

> - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a list that is not closed
